bss.topic: Expansão marítima portuguesa e a chegada de Cabral

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual produto do Oriente os portugueses mais buscavam com as Grandes Navegações?
questions.hint: Pense em pimenta, cravo e canela.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual era o principal destino comercial que motivou a expansão marítima portuguesa?
questions.hint: Era de lá que vinham as especiarias.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual embarcação leve, com velas que permitiam navegar contra o vento, foi muito usada pelos portugueses?
questions.hint: Ela tinha velas triangulares chamadas latinas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual instrumento ajudava os navegadores a calcular a latitude pela posição dos astros?
questions.hint: O nome tem a ver com 'astros'.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano a frota de Pedro Álvares Cabral chegou ao território que hoje é o Brasil?
questions.hint: Foi no fim do século XV, virando para o XVI.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que dia e mês de 1500 a frota de Cabral avistou terra no litoral brasileiro?
questions.hint: Foi em um mês do outono no hemisfério sul.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual foi o primeiro ponto de terra avistado pela frota de Cabral?
questions.hint: O nome lembra uma festa cristã celebrada naquela época do ano.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que atual estado brasileiro a frota de Cabral desembarcou em 1500?
questions.hint: Fica no litoral do Nordeste, onde hoje está Porto Seguro.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Para onde a frota de Cabral seguiu viagem depois de passar pelo Brasil?
questions.hint: Era o destino comercial principal da expedição.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual documento escrito em 1500 descreveu ao rei de Portugal a terra e os povos indígenas encontrados?
questions.hint: Foi escrito pelo escrivão da frota.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual acordo de 1494 dividiu entre Portugal e Espanha as terras descobertas e por descobrir?
questions.hint: O nome vem de uma cidade espanhola.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual nome os portugueses deram primeiro à terra encontrada em 1500?
questions.hint: Eles acharam que era uma ilha e usaram um símbolo cristão.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Qual destes NÃO foi um motivo da expansão marítima portuguesa?
questions.hint: Pense no que existia no século XV.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que Portugal saiu na frente nas Grandes Navegações?
options: Tinha posição atlântica, estabilidade política e investimento em navegação
Tinha a maior população da Europa
Já tinha colônias na América desde o ano 1000
Era o único país com portos
questions.answer: Tinha posição atlântica, estabilidade política e investimento em navegação
questions.hint: Pense na localização do país no mapa da Europa.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que a busca por uma rota marítima para as Índias era tão importante para os comerciantes europeus no século XV?
questions.hint: Pense no preço das especiarias e em quem controlava as rotas por terra.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A Carta de Caminha mostra o olhar dos portugueses sobre os indígenas. Por que é importante lembrar que os indígenas também tinham sua própria visão desse encontro?
questions.hint: Pense em quem escreveu o documento e em quem já vivia na terra.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What does a linear search do?
options: Checks each item in a list one by one
Splits the list in half each time
questions.answer: Checks each item in a list one by one
questions.hint: 'Linear' means in a line.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Where does a linear search usually start?
questions.hint: It goes in order from the beginning.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Does a list need to be sorted before a linear search?
questions.hint: It checks every item anyway.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: When does a linear search stop?
options: When the item is found or the list ends
questions.answer: When the item is found or the list ends
questions.hint: There are two possible reasons.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A linear search looks for 7 in the list [3, 9, 7, 2, 5]. How many comparisons does it make before finding 7?
questions.hint: Count each item it checks, including 7.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A linear search looks for 10 in the list [4, 8, 1, 6]. 10 is not there. How many comparisons does it make?
questions.hint: It must check every item.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the largest number of comparisons a linear search could make on a list of 50 items?
questions.hint: Think about the worst case.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the smallest number of comparisons a linear search could make on a list of 50 items?
questions.hint: Think about the best case.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In Python, which loop is most useful for checking every item in a list?
questions.hint: You want to repeat once for each item.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In Python, which operator compares two values to see if they are equal?
questions.hint: A single '=' assigns a value.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In Python, what keyword is used to send a value back from a function?
questions.hint: It ends the function and gives back a result.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: A linear search function returns -1. What does this usually mean?
options: The item is the first one
questions.hint: -1 can't be a real position in a list.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: In Python, the list is names = ['Ana', 'Leo', 'Mia', 'Raj']. What index does a linear search return for 'Mia'?
questions.hint: Python indexes start at 0.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: What is the output of this code? nums = [5, 2, 8]; found = False; for n in nums: if n == 8: found = True; print(found)
questions.hint: Is 8 in the list?

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Why might a linear search be slow for a very large list?
options: It may need to check every item
It always checks the list twice
It deletes items as it goes
questions.answer: It may need to check every item
questions.hint: Think about a list of one million items.

questions.subject: comp
questions.q: Describe, in steps, how a linear search would find the word 'cat' in the list ['dog', 'fish', 'cat', 'bird'].
questions.hint: Say what happens at each item.

en.topic: Writing articles for magazines and newspapers

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is a headline?
options: The last paragraph of an article
questions.hint: It is printed in large letters at the top.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is a standfirst?
options: A short introduction under the headline
An advert next to the article
questions.answer: A short introduction under the headline
questions.hint: It comes straight after the headline.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the job of a subheading in an article?
options: To break the text into sections
To give the price of the magazine
questions.answer: To break the text into sections
questions.hint: It helps readers find their way.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What does 'readership' mean?
options: The people who read a publication
The person who prints the paper
questions.answer: The people who read a publication
questions.hint: Think of the word 'reader'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which headline uses alliteration?
questions.hint: Look for repeated starting sounds.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which headline uses a pun?
questions.hint: Think about what bread does in the oven.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why do newspaper headlines often use the present tense?
options: To make the news feel immediate
Because the past tense is not allowed
questions.answer: To make the news feel immediate
questions.hint: Compare 'Team Wins Cup' with 'Team Won Cup'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which question words should the first paragraph of a news article usually answer?
questions.hint: These are often called the 5 Ws.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which opening would best engage a teenage readership in a magazine about gaming?
options: Ever wished you could build your own game world?
This article concerns the topic of games.
The following text will discuss several matters.
questions.answer: Ever wished you could build your own game world?
questions.hint: Which one speaks directly to the reader?

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which is an example of direct address?
options: You won't believe what happened next.
questions.answer: You won't believe what happened next.
questions.hint: Look for the word 'you'.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What do we call words placed inside speech marks from a real person in an article?
questions.hint: Journalists use them to add a witness's voice.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which feature is more typical of a magazine article than a newspaper report?
questions.hint: Magazines often feel like a friend talking.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which subheading best fits a section about saving money on school trips?
questions.hint: A good subheading tells you what the section is about.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence would work best as a standfirst for an article about a school garden?
options: Students at one city school have turned a dusty car park into a buzzing garden.
The end of the garden story.
questions.answer: Students at one city school have turned a dusty car park into a buzzing garden.
questions.hint: A standfirst gives a quick taste of the story.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write a headline and a one-sentence standfirst for an article about a new skate park opening in your town.
questions.hint: Make the headline short and catchy.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain how a writer could change an article about healthy eating so that it engages children aged 8 instead of adults.
questions.hint: Think about vocabulary, tone and examples.
